description: New epics E24 to E32. Epics live in PenniLogic/docs and carry no Estimate; their Rollup is the sum of child ticket estimates.

items.title: [EPIC] E24 - Platform, deployment and reliability
items.goal: Own the infrastructure, deployment, backup, disaster-recovery and observability work that E01 explicitly deferred and E19 never picked up, so that no service reaches real user data without a runnable environment, a proven restore and an alert that reaches a human.
scope: Infrastructure as code for every environment; no click-ops
Deploy pipelines with canary, feature flags, kill switches and reversible migrations
Backups, point-in-time recovery, a secondary region and a performed restore drill
OpenTelemetry traces, metrics and logs, SLOs, alert routing and on-call rotation
NTP synchronisation and India-region tamper-evident log retention for CERT-In
Structured log scrubbing so financial values and PII never reach a log sink
out_of_scope: Application-layer cryptography and tenancy isolation (E19)
Kubernetes; the chosen runtime is ECS Fargate per the stack decision
Vendor certification programmes such as SOC 2 or ISO 27001
exit_criteria: Every environment is created from code and can be destroyed and recreated
A restore from backup into a clean account has actually been performed and timed against a written RPO and RTO
Golden-signal dashboards exist and at least one alert has been proven to page the on-call owner
A deliberately planted financial value in a log line fails the CI log-scan gate
A rollback has been rehearsed for each deployable component and the evidence is attached to the release record
traceability: planning-audit-input.md: deployment, IaC, backups, restore, DR, observability, SLOs, alerting and on-call have no owner

items.title: [EPIC] E25 - Quality, verification and release assurance
items.goal: Turn the written test strategy into executable, enforced gates covering the whole verification surface: unit, property, integration, contract and end-to-end; black-box and white-box security testing; SAST and DAST; mutation testing; load, stress and soak; chaos; backup, restore and disaster recovery; accessibility; performance budgets; privacy traffic inspection; penetration testing; and release and rollback evidence. This epic is cross-cutting: its tickets span Sprint 02 to post-beta, and the platform work it consumes is expressed as ticket-level dependencies rather than an epic-level block.
scope: Money-path verification harness: property-based, mutation and independent-model gates plus idempotency and adversarial retry
Provider and consumer contract testing against the published OpenAPI spec
Active cross-tenant, BOLA and authentication attack suites (white-box and black-box)
SAST, DAST, dependency and secret scanning as blocking CI gates, with flaky-test quarantine
Load, stress, soak and chaos suites plus a disaster-recovery game day
Accessibility conformance and performance budgets as CI gates on Android and web
Automated privacy traffic inspection on every release candidate
Threat-model refresh loop, independent penetration test and black-box red-team scenarios
out_of_scope: Writing the feature tests that belong to each feature ticket; this epic owns harnesses, gates and evidence
Certification audits
exit_criteria: Every verification category named in the goal has an owning ticket, a runner and a gate that can fail a pull request or a release
Money-path modules fail CI when the mutation threshold or the independent-model comparison is not met
A release candidate cannot be promoted without accessibility, performance, privacy-capture and rollback evidence
The penetration test has been completed and all high and critical findings are closed and retested
Epic scheduling is nominal: ticket-level dependencies govern order, and no quality ticket is blocked by the epic sprint value
traceability: planning-audit-input.md: load, stress, soak, chaos, restore drills, accessibility, performance budgets, mutation testing, automated privacy inspection, billing replay, AI eval CI, pen test and rollback rehearsals lack executable tickets

items.title: [EPIC] E26 - Architecture decision gates
items.goal: Close the nine architecture decisions that currently force implementers to guess, so that no data-touching ticket is written against an undecided model. Each decision is a dated ADR with a chosen option, rejected options and the migration consequence, published as its own reserved file so the nine can be written in parallel.
scope: Money wire format, time and idempotency conventions
Category model as an append-only reporting dimension
Ledger, foreign exchange and debt-balance derivation
Encryption scope, searchable fields and row-level security
Authentication, passkeys, provider, relying-party identifier, recovery and device binding
Admin boundary: separate process, host, database role, policy boundary and audit stream
Shared-data erasure and cross-user key access
AI egress, runtime platform and Mode C custom endpoints
Entitlement and quota model: plan and feature identity, request and token dimensions, model allowlist, BYOK treatment, usage accounting and reset boundary
Per-decision file layout, reserved numbering ADR-015 to ADR-023, and a generated index so nine records never edit the same lines
out_of_scope: Implementation of any decision; each ADR is followed by its own implementation tickets
Decisions with no current implementation consumer
exit_criteria: All nine ADRs are merged as ADR-015 to ADR-023, each in its own file, dated and linked from the epics and tickets they unblock, with the index and pending table generated rather than hand-edited
Every ADR names the option chosen, the options rejected and the migration cost of reversing it
No ticket in Ready depends on an open ADR
Each ADR lists the tests that will prove the decision was implemented as written
The two conflicting entitlement sketches in the research documents are marked superseded in place by the accepted entitlement record
traceability: architecture/01-domain-model.md section 5 and architecture/03-stack-and-monetization.md section 8 describe entitlements differently; ADR-023 supersedes one of them

items.title: [EPIC] E27 - Launch-blocking compliance floor
items.goal: Land the compliance obligations that legally must exist before the first real person is onboarded, including the closed beta. E20 keeps the post-beta readiness work; this epic carries only what a beta user makes mandatory.
scope: Consent ledger, purpose registry and data-principal rights with a defined service level
Pre-onboarding consent, age gate and permission dashboard on Android
Third-party SDK inventory, payload scrubbing and an accurate Play Data Safety declaration
Privacy policy, terms, disclaimers and processor agreements published before onboarding
CERT-In point of contact, six-hour breach reporting runbook and a rehearsed drill
Retention schedule expressed as enforced jobs rather than a document
out_of_scope: Counsel review of expansion markets and Account Aggregator positioning (E20, E29)
Backend cryptography (E19) and platform log retention (E24)
Epic-level blocking on the whole security epic; the specific security and platform tickets are named as dependencies instead
exit_criteria: No onboarding path exists that does not record a versioned, purpose-specific consent
Access, correction and erasure requests complete end to end within the published service level
The Play Data Safety declaration matches captured traffic and the recorded SDK inventory
The breach drill has been run against the six-hour clock and the gaps found are ticketed
Retention jobs run on a schedule and their effect is observable
Every compliance-floor prerequisite named here is closed and evidenced before the first beta invitation is sent, not before public release
The Data Safety declaration is backed by automated privacy capture evidence produced before beta rather than by a manual questionnaire
traceability: planning-audit-input.md: pre-onboarding DPDP consent/privacy/age/CERT-In/Data Safety work is scheduled after beta

items.title: [EPIC] E28 - Advanced ingestion: email, receipts and cash
items.goal: Extend capture beyond SMS and notifications to the three sources that close the remaining gaps in a user's picture of their money: emailed statements and receipts, photographed paper receipts, and cash spending that no channel will ever report.
scope: On-device email parsing that emits structured events only; raw email content never leaves the handset
On-device receipt capture and text recognition with user confirmation
ATM and cash reconciliation against the manual cash entry that already exists
Extension of source precedence and deduplication to the new sources
Revocable, least-privilege mailbox access with a distinct consent purpose
out_of_scope: Screen scraping or credential sharing with any bank
Account Aggregator connectivity (E29)
Model-generated amounts; every figure is parsed deterministically or confirmed by the user
Server-side email fetching or parsing, permanently
A second manual cash entry surface, which already exists
exit_criteria: Each new source registers with the ingestion pipeline without a change to the existing SMS and notification paths
The same transaction arriving through two sources deduplicates deterministically and the surviving record is explainable
Email access is revocable in the app and revocation stops all fetching, proven by capture
Receipt optical character recognition never writes a transaction without user confirmation
Cash balances reconcile against the ledger with no created or destroyed money
traceability: planning-audit-input.md: receipt OCR, cash handling and email ingestion are missing from the ticket backlog

items.title: [EPIC] E29 - Account Aggregator and open banking readiness
items.goal: Hold Account Aggregator connectivity as a deliberately deferred, fully specified option rather than an unowned assumption, so that the decision to pursue or abandon a Financial Information User role is made on evidence and can be executed without re-planning.
scope: Readiness assessment: role, licensing, cost, consent artefact model and the abandon criteria
Consent, fetch, mapping and revocation implemented behind a default-off kill switch
Mapping of aggregator data onto the existing ledger and ingestion precedence rules
Data minimisation, retention and purpose limitation for aggregator-sourced records
out_of_scope: Any launch of the feature before the readiness assessment is accepted
Holding or moving funds; PenniLogic never acts as a payment processor
Replacing deterministic SMS and notification capture
exit_criteria: A dated assessment records the decision to pursue or defer, with named abandon criteria
The integration is inert by default and enabling it is a deliberate, audited configuration change
Aggregator records carry their consent artefact identifier and expire with the consent
Revoking consent stops fetching and removes derived records within the published service level
traceability: docs/compliance/01-regulatory-landscape.md Account Aggregator and FIU section, ADR-013
planning-audit-input.md: Account Aggregator work is missing from the ticket backlog

items.title: [EPIC] E30 - Globalization and multi-currency
items.goal: Deliver the multi-currency and localization capability that the ledger reserved but deliberately did not implement in the minimum viable product, without weakening the single-currency invariants that protect correctness today.
scope: Foreign exchange clearing accounts and linked exchange groups activated as a real feature
Quoted rate, rate source and explicit fee stored on every cross-currency exchange
Reporting currency selection with derivation that shows the rate used
Localization framework and locale-aware rendering, with INR as the default presentation
Migration of existing single-currency data with no change to stored amounts
Contract slice carrying currency, exchange groups, quoted rates and reporting derivation on the wire
Web rendering slice so multi-currency is not an Android-only capability
out_of_scope: Executing currency conversion or holding balances on a user's behalf
Investment or remittance products
Changing the internal integer minor-unit representation
exit_criteria: A cross-currency exchange is recorded as a linked group whose entries sum to zero per currency
Every converted figure can be traced to a stored rate, a rate source and a stated fee
Formatting happens only at the render boundary and never inside the domain layer
Existing single-currency users see no change in stored amounts or derived balances after migration
traceability: planning-audit-input.md architecture direction item 2 and the INR rendering gap
docs/architecture domain model, currency and ledger sections

items.title: [EPIC] E31 - Program governance and delivery protocol
items.goal: Make the board mechanically trustworthy and make parallel work safe: native dependency edges instead of prose, a Ready state that means what it says, a written protocol for cross-repository change, and an approval model that a single collaborator organisation cannot silently bypass.
scope: Native GitHub dependency edges as the authoritative source, mirrored into ticket bodies
Ready-state reconciliation so a blocked ticket cannot sit in Ready
Definition of Ready and Definition of Done adopted per repository
Cross-repository parallel pull request protocol using expand, migrate and contract sequencing
Independent agent-review governance through separate role sessions, current-head attestations and required policy checks under one GitHub user
Organisation plan capability: branch protection and rulesets on private repositories, proven on a private fixture repository
out_of_scope: Project field schema changes that require renaming existing options without a migration
Any tooling that writes to the board without an audit trail
exit_criteria: Every declared dependency exists as a native blockedBy edge and the reconciliation job reports zero drift
A ticket with an open blocker cannot remain in Ready; the check runs on a schedule and fails loudly
A cross-repository change lands as sequenced pull requests with no window in which either side is broken
No developer agent or developer session can satisfy a required external reviewer-agent attestation
The organisation holds a plan under which branch protection, rulesets and required reviews can be configured on private repositories, evidenced by an API call that previously returned HTTP 403
traceability: planning-audit-input.md: all dependency declarations are body prose; GitHub blockedBy has zero edges
planning-audit-input.md: the organization has one collaborator and no teams
T-EXT-01: GitHub Team capability verified on 2026-09-02 with an active private-repository ruleset, required review and required status check; temporary fixture removed

items.title: [EPIC] E32 - Server sync and offline data plane
items.goal: Give the offline-first client a real, owned server contract. Today the Android sync queue has no counterpart: no change feed, no cursor semantics, no conflict rules and no tenancy story for the sync path.
scope: Sync engine decision recorded before any implementation
Change feed, cursor and watermark semantics with idempotent apply
Deterministic conflict resolution rules per entity, including deletes and money-bearing records
Tenancy isolation on the sync path, including connection-pooler session safety
Client reconciliation, backoff and poison-message handling
out_of_scope: Real-time collaborative editing
Syncing derived projections that the client can recompute
Adopting a hosted sync vendor without the recorded decision
exit_criteria: A client that has been offline through a schema change can converge without data loss
Concurrent edits resolve to the same result on every device, proven by a replay test
A sync request cannot read another tenant's rows, proven by an active attack test under pooled connections
Replaying a change batch twice produces no duplicate ledger effect
traceability: planning-audit-input.md: server sync contracts and ownership are missing

items.title: [EPIC] E33 - Experience strategy, research and design operations
items.goal: Establish the user evidence, experience architecture, decision rights and artifact operations that let a large design organization plan the complete product before frontend implementation without turning design into an unversioned waterfall.
scope: Chief Design Officer governance, RACI, review queues, approval expiry and decision log
Research ethics, recruitment, repository, personas, jobs, mental models and baseline evidence
Journey maps, service blueprints, platform allocation, sitemaps and navigation
Machine-readable screen, flow, component, diagram and traceability registry
Visual and interaction direction selected through evidence and accessibility review
Figma project, file, branch, library, versioning and archival topology
UX outcome metrics, continuous research and design-debt governance
out_of_scope: Production component implementation
Choosing legal or financial policy in a design artifact
Treating unvalidated persona hypotheses as market evidence
exit_criteria: Every persona, journey, flow, screen, component family and required diagram has a stable identifier and owner
Android, web and admin sitemaps and platform allocation are approved by the IA Lead
The CDO has approved one visual and interaction direction with rejected options and risks recorded
Research evidence, limitations and resulting changes are traceable to backlog tickets
Figma and decision governance are operational before parallel platform design begins
traceability: User request: complete personas, stories, journeys, sitemaps, screens, components and flows before frontend work

items.title: [EPIC] E34 - Cross-platform design system, content and handoff
items.goal: Publish one governed semantic design and content system with explicit Android, web and admin adaptations, complete component states, accessibility, localization and design-to-code contracts before any product frontend consumes local values or invented patterns.
scope: Brand, token, typography, icon, illustration, data-visualization, grid, motion and haptic foundations
Navigation, action, input, financial-data, collection, feedback, overlay, trust and operator component families
Light, dark, high-contrast, large-text, zoom, responsive and adaptive behavior
Canonical terminology, content patterns, regulated-copy approval and localization
Versioned libraries, contribution model, deprecation and breaking-change policy
Token packages, component specs, Code Connect mapping, assets and implementation handoff
out_of_scope: One visual implementation shared unchanged across platforms
Marketing-site design
Frontend code owned by Android, web or admin repositories
exit_criteria: Every registered component family has required variants, states, content limits and accessibility behavior
All semantic tokens resolve in supported themes and platform transformations
Money and status meaning never relies on color alone and every chart has a text or table equivalent
Android, web and admin can consume versioned tokens and mapped component specifications
The CDO, Accessibility Lead and Design Systems Lead approve the release

items.title: [EPIC] E35 - Android experience design
items.goal: Design and validate every native Android journey, screen, system handoff and adaptive state as a coherent Material 3 product before the Android application shell or feature frontend is implemented.
scope: Compact, medium and expanded navigation and shell
Identity, onboarding, consent, permissions, recovery and capture health
Debt, transactions, planning, goals, net worth and reporting
Split, family, AI, billing, trust, support and notification preferences
Offline, process-death, deep-link, restricted-setting, privacy and coercion states
Complete interactive prototype, usability evidence and implementation handoff
out_of_scope: Android service and parser implementation
Copying desktop web layouts onto tablets
Using non-Material controls where a native control exists
exit_criteria: Every Android registry screen and flow has a versioned D6 artifact and mapped implementation ticket
Critical journeys pass prototype accessibility, usability, financial-comprehension and safe-exit gates
Compact and expanded behavior, predictive Back, edge-to-edge and largest text scale are demonstrated
No Android UI implementation ticket is startable without its exact design dependency
The Android Design Lead and CDO approve the complete platform handoff
traceability: All Android story and task tickets

items.title: [EPIC] E36 - Customer web experience design
items.goal: Design and validate every responsive customer-web journey, page, dense financial workflow and recovery path before the web shell or feature frontend is implemented.
scope: Authentication, recovery, responsive shell and overview
Transactions, bulk management, imports, clarification and export
Debt, income, budgets, goals, net worth, holdings and reports
Split, family, AI, billing, preferences, trust and support
Keyboard, screen-reader, zoom, narrow-layout, browser and failure states
Complete interactive prototype, usability evidence and implementation handoff
out_of_scope: Admin/operator experience
Marketing-site acquisition pages
A mobile-web experience that only redirects to Android
exit_criteria: Every customer-web registry page and flow has a versioned D6 artifact and mapped implementation ticket
Bulk, import, debt comparison and export tasks pass usability and comprehension thresholds
Every journey is keyboard complete and usable at 200 percent zoom
No customer-web frontend ticket is startable without its exact design dependency
The Web Design Lead and CDO approve the complete platform handoff
traceability: All web story and task tickets

items.title: [EPIC] E37 - Admin and operator experience design
items.goal: Design and validate the complete least-privilege operator product, including queues, approvals, audit, rights, support, billing and incidents, before an admin frontend can expose a capability or normalize unsafe access.
scope: Operator personas, roles, permission-aware sitemap and absent-route behavior
Plans, features, quotas, providers and spend controls
Support, customer status, refunds, rights and grievance queues
Redaction, unmask, elevation, export and four-eyes decisions
Audit, access monitoring, aggregate analytics, incidents and break-glass
Failure, SLA-clock, accessibility, density and performance behavior
Complete operator prototype, simulation evidence and implementation handoff
out_of_scope: A browse-all customer or transaction explorer
Direct database, backup or KMS access
Combining admin and customer authentication or navigation
exit_criteria: Every operator capability is present only for an authorized role and absent otherwise
Every high-risk action demonstrates provenance, requester/approver separation, expiry, audit and notification
Statutory-clock, incident and unavailable-dependency simulations pass without an unsafe shortcut
No admin frontend ticket is startable without its exact design dependency
The Admin Design Lead, Security, Accessibility Lead and CDO approve the handoff

items.title: [EPIC] E38 - Experience validation and design quality assurance
items.goal: Operate an independent design-quality lifecycle that tests coverage, usability, accessibility, comprehension, privacy, localization, design-to-code conformance and release readiness rather than allowing designers or developers to approve their own output.
scope: Registry, traceability, component and token lint
Heuristic review, cognitive walkthrough and prototype accessibility
Android, web and admin moderated usability
Financial comprehension, content and localization validation
Household privacy, coercion, authorization and operator-abuse scenarios
Design-to-code visual, interaction and semantic regression
Cross-platform parity, UAT, release design QA and post-launch research
out_of_scope: Financial engine correctness testing
Security penetration testing owned by E25
Self-certification by the artifact author
exit_criteria: Every critical flow has an independent prototype test and implementation-level UAT owner
Every platform passes its accessibility and usability gates before D6 handoff
Built screens match approved artifacts or carry an approved documented deviation
Private beta and public launch require unexpired D8 design evidence
The Design QA Lead and CDO can inspect coverage and open findings from Project views
traceability: E25 engineering and security verification gates
